paper.title_en: Testing PPN by the Rotation of S301 Star
paper.abstract_en: The recently discovered S301 star, with an orbital period of 8.7 years and eccentricity $e = 0.982$, reaches a pericenter of just $140\, R_{\mathrm{s}}$--- approximately nine times closer than S2's $\sim 1200R_{\mathrm{s}}$ ---offering an unprecedented laboratory for testing gravity at large post-Newtonian counting parameters. We demonstrate that S301's stellar spin precession provides a novel probe of the PPN parameter $γ$, scaling as $(2γ_{\mathrm{PPN}} + 1)/3$ relative to general relativity (GR). For maximum projected velocity shifts of $46.1~{\rm km\,s^{-1}}$, next-generation spectrographs could constrain $γ_{\mathrm{PPN}}$ to $\sim10\%$ precision; this forecast is conditional on the treatment of astrophysical systematics. When combined with S301's orbital precession --- a substantial $\sim 1.95^\circ$ pericenter advance per orbit (GR prediction), approximately an order of magnitude larger than S2's $\sim 0.2^\circ$, constraining $(2γ_{\mathrm{PPN}} - β_{\mathrm{PPN}}+2)/3$ --- the spin measurement breaks the $β$-$γ$ degeneracy. A projected MCMC analysis of S2 and S301 observations yields $σ_{2γ-β}\approx 3\times 10^{-2}$ from the orbital precession and $σ_β\approx 3\times 10^{-2}$ (with $γ$ fixed to its GR value by the spin measurement; $σ_β\approx0.10$ if the spin uncertainty is propagated), with the $γ$ precision limited by the spin precession measurement to $σ_γ\approx 0.1$. While the spin precession provides an independent consistency check, its true significance lies in probing the same PPN parameters at unprecedentedly large counting parameters, where the non-linear and velocity-dependent PPN terms are comparatively enhanced.
